claims.statement: Open SWE's backend is a LangGraph application that serves six graphs (agent, reviewer, analyzer, review-scout, chat, scheduler) together with the FastAPI app (agent.webapp:app), all wired through langgraph.json which also declares the checkpointer TTL policy and .env env file.

make dev starts a local Postgres service when POSTGRES_URI is absent, rejects an occupied port 2024, then runs `uv run langgraph dev --no-browser --port 2024 --n-jobs-per-worker 10`, serving all graphs plus the FastAPI app on one process.

make run runs `uvicorn agent.webapp:app --reload --port 8000` and serves the FastAPI app without the LangGraph runtime, which is insufficient for dashboard features that create LangGraph runs; full local dev therefore requires make dev on :2024.

make install installs backend dependencies including dev extras via `uv sync --extra dev`, and the Makefile exposes uv-run wrappers for pytest (test/integration_tests), ruff (lint/format/format-check), and ty (typecheck) over the repository or agent and tests.

langgraph.json and local uv constraints use the 0.15.0rc1 LangGraph API/runtime line, while the standalone Docker image remains based on langgraph-api 0.13.3-py3.14 and configures its registrations through environment variables.

langgraph.desktop.json is a separate trimmed deployment manifest for the desktop build that exposes only the agent graph, disables the built-in UI, and configures a local auth handler (agent.local_auth:auth) with Studio auth disabled.
The dashboard is part of a pnpm workspace whose members are ui, desktop, and tests/e2e, and Turborepo orchestrates the per-package dev, build, typecheck, test, and check tasks.

make web runs the root dashboard dev script, which invokes `turbo run dev --filter=open-swe-dashboard`; the dashboard Vite server defaults to port 3000 and proxies backend paths to DASHBOARD_API_URL, defaulting to http://localhost:2024.
The dashboard build/typecheck/test scripts fan out across the workspace through Turborepo, while lint (oxlint) and format/format:check (oxfmt) run once from the repo root and are not Turborepo tasks.
Turborepo's build task caches .output/**, .vercel/output/**, and build/**, and treats DASHBOARD_API_URL, SOURCE_COMMIT, VERCEL, E2E_HARNESS, and any VITE_* variable as cache-affecting build inputs.

The experimental Electron desktop app bundles the compiled dashboard UI and a local backend, connects cloud features to a selected backend, and supports local-agent work through a private loopback LangGraph server; packaged builds ask for and store a backend URL rather than defaulting to a hosted deployment.

make install-desktop installs or updates Open SWE Desktop on macOS by refusing to run with a dirty working tree, fast-forwarding to main, then invoking scripts/install_desktop.sh, whereas make install-checkout runs that script against the current checkout without touching git state.

scripts/install_desktop.sh is macOS-only, verifies node, ditto, uv, and a pnpm/corepack launcher are present, packs the desktop app, and atomically swaps it into /Applications (or ~/Applications when /Applications is not writable).

scripts/create_sandbox_snapshot.py builds a LangSmith sandbox snapshot from a Docker image using SandboxClient and prints the resulting UUID for selection as a workspace base snapshot from the dashboard.

scripts/purge_wakeup_crons.py is a one-time backfill that can dry-run or delete expired one-shot thread_wakeup crons from a deployment, resolving the deployment URL from --url or LANGGRAPH_URL and the API key from LANGGRAPH_API_KEY or LANGSMITH_API_KEY.

The root Dockerfile builds the standalone production LangGraph API server image (not the sandbox image) from langchain/langgraph-api:0.13.3-py3.14, installing the repository with uv and baking six graph registrations, HTTP app (agent.webapp:app), and checkpointer TTL into LANGSERVE_GRAPHS, LANGGRAPH_HTTP, and LANGGRAPH_CHECKPOINTER; it exposes port 8000.

A standalone backend container requires the Agent Server backing services and settings — DATABASE_URI (Postgres), REDIS_URI (Redis), LANGSMITH_API_KEY, and LANGGRAPH_CLOUD_LICENSE_KEY — plus LANGGRAPH_URL set to the public backend URL, and must not use scale-to-zero hosting because background runs rely on Redis/Postgres-backed workers staying available.

ui/Dockerfile is a multi-stage Node 24 build (run from the repo root) that installs the workspace with the frozen pnpm lockfile, builds open-swe-dashboard into a Nitro .output server, runs it on port 8080, and reads the backend it fronts from DASHBOARD_API_URL at runtime so one image serves any deployment.

In a separate dashboard deployment, the dashboard proxies browser /dashboard/api/* requests and backend-prefixed routes to the backend while preserving cookies and OAuth redirects; a direct cross-origin browser alternative uses VITE_DASHBOARD_API_BASE_URL and requires the dashboard origin in DASHBOARD_ALLOWED_ORIGINS.

The backend can alternatively be deployed to LangGraph Platform by connecting the repository and setting the same application environment, using the hosted deployment URL for LANGGRAPH_URL and webhook callbacks.

The production Nitro proxy requires DASHBOARD_API_URL at request time and throws if it is unset, rather than falling back to a backend; it proxies the original path and query while preserving OAuth redirects manually.

The FastAPI app rejects a wildcard DASHBOARD_ALLOWED_ORIGINS configuration because credentials are enabled, and applies the configured origins to credentialed CORS with dashboard, plan, workflow, webhook, and health routers installed.

The backend can serve a bundled dashboard from DASHBOARD_STATIC_DIR or an in-repository ui/.output/public build, while explicitly declining reserved API and LangGraph paths so its UI catch-all cannot shadow them; a configured Vite development URL replaces the static build for same-origin hot reload.

Dashboard asset and client-router paths must be built with DASHBOARD_BASE_PATH equal to a LangGraph http.mount_prefix; the platform manifest derives that build value from its mount prefix, while local builds require it to be supplied.

make tunnel requires NGROK_DOMAIN and exposes local port 2024 through an ngrok policy that returns 404 for every path outside /webhooks/*, protecting unauthenticated LangGraph development routes from public exposure.

The root Docker image does not itself build the dashboard; standalone Docker serving needs a prebuilt dashboard in the repository or DASHBOARD_STATIC_DIR, whereas the platform manifest performs a best-effort dashboard build and continues backend deployment if it fails.

A standalone backend using LANGGRAPH_AUTH_TYPE=noop exposes raw LangGraph routes to network clients; deployments should use LangSmith authentication or an authenticated/private network boundary because dashboard sessions and webhook signatures protect only custom routes.

scripts/stamp_build_info.py writes a UTC build timestamp and optional SOURCE_COMMIT to open-swe-build-info.json, and when given a dashboard directory records the SHA-256 of its build stamp in the backend sidecar.

scripts/rebuild_transcript_projections.py repairs named transcript read projections by replaying each thread's event log from POSTGRES_URI, without changing attachments, tool outputs, or the thread version, and returns failure when any requested rebuild fails.
make migration delegates to scripts/new_migration.py, which generates the next numbered Alembic revision and chains it to the current migration head.

The local Compose PostgreSQL service is a postgres:16 container bound to 127.0.0.1:5433 with a named open-swe-postgres volume and a readiness healthcheck, so local database data survives container removal.
